synopsis: Co-simulation combines separate simulation programs in step: FMI standardizes their connections, FMUs package individual models, and SSP records connections and parameters so arrangements can be shared and reproduced [f13230, f13234]. The booklet treats FMI/SSP as domain-neutral and suitable for off-road work, with about 250 FMI-supporting tools reported by mid-2025, although Chapter 9 says the research did not verify FMI/SSP's status [f7167, f8336, f7165]. Practical applications include connecting reduced-order machine models to high-fidelity components and coupling Mevea with Simulink through FMI or TCP/IP [f6395, f8562, f8699]. When sensor internals are unavailable, the recommendation is to request a black-box OSI/OSMP FMU using FMI 2.0; secure black-box exchange approaches existed in 2024, but cited independent lidar-model examples are on-road evidence [f4857, f4858, f4504, f6381]. Standards do not eliminate integration risk: coordinate systems, clocks, synchronized machine pose and material semantics still need alignment, specialist integration requires co-simulation expertise, and the lowest-cost Chrono-to-Isaac heavy-machine chain is not turnkey or qualification-ready without major work [f13237, f8729, f8758, f9280].
